# 2 Baruch Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**1** Then I answered and said: "Lord, my Lord — is this why I was born into the world? To witness what happens to my homeland?

**2** Please, my Lord — if I have found favor with you, take my life away first, so I can go to my ancestors and not have to watch Jerusalem's destruction.

**3** Two things weigh on me more than I can bear: I cannot stand by while God's wrath falls on Zion, and I cannot bear seeing my own people dragged off into captivity.

**4** But let me ask you one thing, Lord: What will happen to your Law? Will the Law go into exile with Zion?

**5** Will the priests who served before you be taken away? Will the lampstand be put out? Will the incense no longer rise?

**6** Will the daily offerings stop? Will the songs of praise fall silent?

**7** Everything you told me about this city — where is it now?

**8** If you destroy your own city and hand your land over to those who hate us, how will Israel's name survive?

**9** How will we ever speak your praises again? Who will be left to study your Law?"

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. "Homeland" for "mother" contextualizes the personification. Rhetorical questions in vv.5-6 restructured as parallel short sentences for impact. V.9 brings out the communal dimension of Torah loss.*
